reapack.name: ClearAutomation.lua
reapack.desc: Clear automation points on selected track

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Clear Automation}\line Deletes envelope points (Volume, Pan, Width) from the selected track.\line \line {\b Modes:}\line - Between : inside the time selection\line - Left : to the left of the selection\line - Right : to the right of the selection\line - Outside : everything outside the selection\line - Whole : the entire track\line \line {\b How to use:}\line 1. Select a track in REAPER\line 2. Make a time selection on the timeline\line 3. Run the script\line 4. Choose the mode and envelopes to clear\line 5. Click CLEAR\line \line Requires ReaImGui.}

reapack.name: RandomAutomation.lua
reapack.desc: Random automation generator for selected track

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Random Automation Generator}\line Generates random automation points on Volume, Pan and/or Width envelopes within the time selection.\line \line {\b Parameters:}\line - Enable/disable Pan, Volume, Width\line - Number of points to generate\line - Auto or manual spacing (in seconds)\line - Pan amplitude (%)\line - Volume min/max values (dB)\line - Width amplitude (%)\line \line {\b How to use:}\line 1. Select a track\line 2. Make a time selection\line 3. Run the script\line 4. Set the parameters in the dialog\line 5. Click OK to generate (window stays open to run again)\line \line No ReaImGui required.}

reapack.name: ExtendItems.lua
reapack.desc: Extend item edge to a target position

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Extend Items}\line Moves the left or right edge of selected items to a precise position.\line \line {\b Target positions:}\line - Timeline Zero : moves the edge to 0:00\line - Timecode : enter minutes / seconds / centiseconds manually\line - Bar number : enter a bar number\line \line {\b How to use:}\line 1. Select one or more items on the timeline\line 2. Run the script\line 3. Choose which edge to extend (left or right)\line 4. Choose the target position\line 5. Click EXTEND\line \line Built-in Undo/Redo button included.\line Requires ReaImGui.}

reapack.name: TemplatePicker.lua
reapack.desc: Project template picker with search bar

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Template Picker}\line Browse and quickly load a REAPER project template from a searchable list.\line \line {\b How to use:}\line 1. Run the script\line 2. Use the search bar to filter templates\line 3. Click a template to select it\line 4. Click OPEN or double-click the name\line \line {\b Configuration:}\line The script auto-detects your REAPER ProjectTemplates folder.\line If it does not work, edit TEMPLATE_PATH at the top of the file.\line \line Requires ReaImGui.}

{\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Short Film Project Manager}\line Navigate a short film project folder structure and open .rpp files directly.\line \line {\b Expected folder structure:}\line SHORT_FILMS / MY_FILM_C1 / MY_FILM_Zik / scene01A / scene01A.rpp\line \line {\b Configuration:}\line Edit court_metrage_path at the top of the file:\line - Windows : "D:\\MY_PROJECTS\\SHORT_FILMS"\line - macOS : "/Users/your_name/Projects/Short_Films"\line \line Requires ReaImGui.}

reapack.name: MixMasterCheatSheet.lua
reapack.desc: Mix and mastering cheat sheet by instrument and genre

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 \fswiss Helvetica;}} {\b Mix and Mastering Cheat Sheet}\line Reference interface with recommended EQ, compression and reverb settings for each instrument, organized by musical genre.\line \line {\b Genres:} Rock, Hip-Hop, Jazz, Electronic, and more.\line {\b Instruments:} Drums (Kick, Snare, Hi-Hats, Overhead, Toms), Bass, Guitars, Vocals, Keys.\line \line {\b How to use:}\line 1. Run the script\line 2. Select the musical genre\line 3. Browse by instrument to see EQ / Compressor / Reverb suggestions\line \line This is a reference tool — values are starting points, not rules. Trust your ears!\line \line Requires ReaImGui.}
